title: Hopeless
novel: Barney wanted to [[bond|bond]] with his father Jerome, but he felt that his own life was not [[impressive|impress]] enough. He asked the gang to help him lie to make his life seem more [[exciting|excite]] and [[glamorous|glamorous]]. Ted was asked to pretend he was a famous architect. Robin was told to act like a television star. Marshall and Lily were supposed to pretend they were wealthy [[philanthropists|philanthropist]]. Barney even gave everyone [[fake|fake]] backstories and rehearsed them before the dinner. When Jerome arrived with his new family, Barney put on his best performance. He told [[exaggerated|exaggerate]] stories about his adventures and made his friends sound like [[celebrities|celebrity]]. The gang played along, though they felt [[uncomfortable|uncomfortable]] lying to a man who was trying to have an honest relationship with his son. During the dinner, Jerome's other son, J.J., talked about his school and his friends. Barney felt a [[surge|surge]] of jealousy. He realized that J.J. had grown up with the father that Barney never had. After dinner, Barney took his father aside and finally told the truth. He said that he was not a successful businessman or a hero. He was just a guy who wore suits and chased women. Jerome listened quietly and then told Barney that he did not need to be [[extraordinary|extraordinary]] to be loved. He said he was proud of Barney simply because he was his son. Barney was [[moved|move]] by these words but could not bring himself to fully forgive his father. Later, Barney told the gang that he wanted to go to a casino and gamble his [[sorrows|sorrow]] away. They all went together and had a wild night. By morning, they were exhausted but oddly [[content|content]]. Barney realized that even though his relationship with his father was far from perfect, at least he had his friends, and that was something truly [[hopeless|hopeless]] to give up on.

bond.en: to form a close relationship with someone

impress.en: to make someone admire or respect you

excite.en: to make someone feel eager and happy

glamorous.en: attractive and exciting in a luxurious way

philanthropist.en: a person who gives money to help others

fake.en: not real and made to trick people

exaggerate.en: to make something seem larger or better than it is

celebrity.en: a famous person known by many people

uncomfortable.en: not feeling relaxed or at ease

surge.en: a sudden strong feeling or increase

move.en: to affect someone with strong emotion

content.en: happy and satisfied with what you have

hopeless.en: having no hope or chance of success
